title: Extending an adjoint from an epimorphic generating class
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] and $R:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ an additive functor. Suppose a class $\mathcal P$ of objects of $\mathcal B$ has the following properties: every object of $\mathcal B$ is the target of an epimorphism from an object of $\mathcal P$; and for every $P\in\mathcal P$ there is an object $L_P\in\mathcal A$ and bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(L_P,A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(P,R(A))$, natural in $A\in\mathcal A$. Then $R$ has a left adjoint $L:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$.

proof.text: Choose the stipulated $L_P$ and natural bijections $\theta_{P,X}$ for $P\in\mathcal P$. Put $i_P=\theta_{P,L_P}(\mathrm{id}_{L_P})$, as in the presentation lemma. For an arbitrary $B\in\mathcal B$, apply [lem-trf-partial-adjoint-generator-presentation]. It supplies a cokernel presentation $P_2\xrightarrow{d}P_1\xrightarrow{q}B$, with both terms in $\mathcal P$, and the relation $D:L_{P_2}\to L_{P_1}$ characterized by $\theta_{P_2,L_{P_1}}(D)=i_{P_1}\circ d$. Its conclusions give $\theta_{P,X}(0)=0$ and $\theta_{P_2,X}(a\circ D)=\theta_{P_1,X}(a)\circ d$ for every $X,a$. The hypotheses are precisely the given epimorphic cover and natural corepresentations; projectivity is not needed.

source.place: Tag 0793, lemma-partially-defined-adjoint, proof: first paragraph and the exact presentation in the second paragraph.

proof.text: Take a cokernel $c:L_{P_1}\to C_B$ of $D$, which exists in $\mathcal A$ by [def-sp-abelian]. Apply [lem-trf-cokernel-corepresenting-bijection] with $L_i=L_{P_i}$ and $\theta_{i,X}=\theta_{P_i,X}$. Step 1 gives its cokernel hypothesis for $q$, its zero compatibility for both $\theta_i$, and its relation formula for $D$; target naturality is part of the stipulated $\theta$. The conclusion supplies bijections $\psi_{B,X}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(C_B,X)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(B,R(X))$, characterized by $\psi_{B,X}(v)\circ q=\theta_{P_1,X}(v\circ c)$ and natural in $X$. Thus the required covariant Hom functor is corepresentable for every $B$.

source.place: Tag 0793, lemma-partially-defined-adjoint, proof: last paragraph, the cokernel and the displayed Hom identifications.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-right-adjoint-from-objectwise-representability] with $\mathcal C=\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$, $\mathcal D=\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $F=R^{\mathrm{op}}$. For $Y=B^{\mathrm{op}}$, its presheaf $X\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}}(R^{\mathrm{op}}X,B^{\mathrm{op}})$ is exactly $A\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(B,R(A))$, represented on $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$ by $C_B^{\mathrm{op}}$ through step 2. The cited criterion supplies a right adjoint $G:\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$ and its natural Hom bijections. Reversing arrows gives $L=G^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(L(B),A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(B,R(A))$ natural in both variables, as required. Functor categories may be formed in a containing universe as in the cited criterion.
